title: Replace hand-rolled mime_parser.rs multipart splitting with mailparse subparts
description:
The current mime_parser.rs uses mailparse only for header parsing, then re-implements RFC 2046 multipart boundary splitting manually via split_on_boundary(). This is the source of bt5.12 (bare LF) and the nested multipart gap.

mailparse (already a dependency in core, reader, and mail crates) handles all of this correctly:
- ParsedMail.subparts gives a recursive MIME tree
- Handles bare LF line endings by design
- Handles nested multipart recursion
- Active: v0.15 Nov 2024

Fix: replace split_on_boundary() and flat part iteration with a recursive walk of ParsedMail::subparts, accumulating (Cid, Vec<u8>) blocks depth-first. The public API (parse_mime → Option<ParsedMime>) and the MimeNode/block output format stay the same; only the internal parsing mechanism changes.

No new dependency needed. Do NOT use mail-parser — its API flattens the MIME tree into text/html/attachments, losing the structural information needed for IPLD block construction.

Acceptance: bt5.12 is resolved. Nested multipart/mixed articles produce correct block trees. Bare-LF articles are accepted, not silently dropped.
